reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure. Write gamma_E for the measure defined by stdGaussian E. Concretely, if (e_k) is the standard orthonormal basis used in the definition, gamma_E is the pushforward of the finite product of real Gaussian laws gaussianReal(0,1) by (z_k) -> sum_k z_k e_k. The supplied density fixes each coordinate law as (2*pi)^(-1/2) exp(-t^2/2) dt: the mean is zero and the variance is one. Thus the Gaussian normalization is specified, not an unspecified scale. All integrals below are real Bochner/Lebesgue integrals over the whole E with respect to this same gamma_E.

For every scalar function f:E -> R and every fixed vector v in E, assume:
 (1) f is real Frechet differentiable at every x in E;
 (2) f is integrable with respect to gamma_E;
 (3) x -> <x,v> f(x) is integrable with respect to gamma_E;
 (4) x -> Df(x)[v] is integrable with respect to gamma_E.
Here Df(x):E ->L_R R is the Frechet derivative. The supplied Differentiable and DifferentiableAt definitions assert existence of an actual derivative at every point, and HasFDerivAt.fderiv identifies the literal fderiv_R f x with that derivative. Hence the right-hand integrand is the real linear derivative applied to the same fixed v.

Then
 integral_E <x,v> f(x) d gamma_E(x)
   = integral_E Df(x)[v] d gamma_E(x).

All three integrability conditions are explicit assumptions and are retained in this reconstruction. They mean almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the absolute value for these real functions. Differentiability holds everywhere, not only almost everywhere; continuity of the derivative, a C^1 hypothesis, compact support, boundary decay, and integrability of the entire derivative norm are not additional premises. The directional derivative integrability is for this chosen v only, not simultaneously for every direction. The vector v is arbitrary, with no nonzero or unit-norm restriction. There is no positive-dimension premise. There are no existential constants, error bounds, time horizons or limits. The conclusion is an equality of two finite real integrals, not a pointwise equality of the integrands or an equality of chosen quotient representatives.
objects: A finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its Borel measurable structure; its concretely defined standard Gaussian gamma_E; an arbitrary scalar function f:E->R; one fixed arbitrary vector v:E; the Frechet derivative Df(x):E->L_R R.
domains: E may have any finite dimension, including zero. f and both integrands take values in R. x ranges over all E. v ranges over E without a nonzero or unit-norm condition. All integrability and integrals use gamma_E and the same Borel measurable structure.
quantifiers: For every E with the listed compatible norm, real inner product, finite-dimensional and Borel structures, every f:E->R and v:E, assume everywhere Differentiable_R(f), then Integrable_gamma_E(f), then Integrable_gamma_E(x -> <x,v>f(x)), then Integrable_gamma_E(x -> Df(x)[v]); conclude the one integral equality. All integrability hypotheses are specialized to the already chosen f and v.
assumptions: Exactly the carrier structures, finite dimension and BorelSpace; everywhere real Frechet differentiability of f; and the three separate real L1 conditions f, <.,v>f and Df(.)[v]. No continuous derivative, C^1 regularity, compact support, boundary decay, nonzero v, unit v or whole-derivative-norm integrability is assumed.
conclusion: Integral over E of <x,v>f(x) against gamma_E equals integral over E of Df(x)[v] against gamma_E. Integrability is assumed, not asserted as a new conclusion.
scopes: Differentiability at every point of E. L1 conditions include a.e. strong measurability and finite absolute integrals under gamma_E. The conclusion is a finite scalar integral equality over all E, not a pointwise integrand identity. No Lp quotient representative, time interval, horizon or convergence mode is involved.
constant_dependencies: No existential constant or quantitative estimate. Gaussian mean is 0 and coordinate variance is exactly 1. The directional factor uses v itself with no division by ||v||. The equality has coefficient +1 on both sides and no dimension-dependent prefactor.

definition_reconstruction.stdGaussian: Pushforward of the product of gaussianReal 0 1 laws through the orthonormal-basis synthesis map sum_k z_k e_k.
definition_reconstruction.gaussianReal_variance_convention: gaussianReal mu a is dirac mu when a=0; otherwise it is volume.withDensity of ENNReal.ofReal[(sqrt(2*pi*a))^-1 exp(-(t-mu)^2/(2*a))]. At the used values mu=0,a=1 this is the standard variance-one real Gaussian.
definition_reconstruction.Differentiable: For every x, DifferentiableAt_R f x, meaning existence of a continuous real linear map satisfying HasFDerivAt at x.
definition_reconstruction.fderiv: The literal fderiv is opaque in its printed definition, but the supplied HasFDerivAt.fderiv theorem identifies it with the actual derivative wherever the derivative exists. hf gives this at every x, so no default off-differentiability value enters.
definition_reconstruction.directional_integrand: Apply the continuous real linear map fderiv_R f x to the fixed v; this is not a derivative with respect to v.
definition_reconstruction.Integrable: AEStronglyMeasurable plus HasFiniteIntegral, using the ordinary real norm shown in the fully explicit statement.
definition_reconstruction.unused_shared_context: Hermite/aeval and fderivWithin definitions are supplied in the common context but do not occur in this target and create no additional premise or conclusion.

shared_context_verification.method: Exact UTF-8 text equality and SHA256 comparison; common context read once.
